title: Unsafe code
description: unsafe, pointers, and interop in C#

exercises.title: Declare a Pointer
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to an int named 'ptr' that points to a variable 'x' with value 42. Print the pointer value using Console.WriteLine(ptr).
exercises.starter_code:
using System;

unsafe { int x = 42; int* ptr = &x; /* Console.WriteLine(*ptr); */ }
hints: Wrap fixed blocks/`unsafe { int* ptr = &x; }` per project AllowUnsafeBlocks settings.
Dereference with `*ptr` for scalar printing when address text is undesired.

exercises.title: Dereference a Pointer
exercises.description: Create a pointer to an int and use the * operator to access and Console.WriteLine the value it points to.
exercises.starter_code:
using System;

unsafe { int value = 100; /* dereference */ }
hints: Ensure `/unsafe` is enabled wherever required by the harness.

exercises.title: Pass Pointer to Function
exercises.description: Write a function 'modify' that takes a pointer to int and doubles its value. Call it with a variable and Console.WriteLine the result.
exercises.starter_code:
// Modify(ref num);

static void Modify(ref int p) { }
hints: Managed-friendly alternative: pass `ref int` so callee mutates callers without raw pointers.
Prefer `static void Modify(ref int p)` doubling in-place.

exercises.title: Use the new Keyword
exercises.description: Use the 'new' keyword to allocate a new int pointer, assign a value to it, and Console.WriteLine the dereferenced value.
exercises.starter_code:
using System;

unsafe { /* int* ptr = new int; */ }
hints: Pin unmanaged memory (`Marshal.AllocHGlobal`) when simulating heap pointers.
Always balance allocations with `.FreeHGlobal` in real programs.
Prefer `sizeof(int)` for clarity when requesting native buffers.

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string). Create a pointer to Person using & and set Name to "Bob". Print Name through the pointer.
exercises.starter_code:
// ref Person

class Person { public string Name = ""; }
hints: Reference types/`class Person` idiomatically use managed references—not `*`—when possible.
Use object initializer syntax `{ Name = "Bob" }` when constructing instances.

exercises.title: Nil Pointer Check
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to int named ptr without initializing it. Check if it is nil and Console.WriteLine "nil" or the dereferenced value.
exercises.starter_code:
using System;

unsafe { int* ptr = null; /* check */ }
hints: Compare unmanaged pointers against `null` before dereferencing.
Print literal nil when graders expect pointer-absent text.

exercises.title: Swap with Pointers
exercises.description: Write a function swap(a, b *int) that swaps the values at the two pointers. Call with x:=5, y:=10 and Console.WriteLine after swapping.
exercises.starter_code:
// Swap(ref x, ref y);

static void Swap(ref int a, ref int b) { }
hints: Swap via `(a, b) = (b, a)` with `ref` parameters or traditional temp variable juggling.
Keep method `static void Swap(ref int a, ref int b)` for readability.
